newsitem.title: USA: Northrop's B-2 bomber flights suspended.
newsitem.headline: Northrop's B-2 bomber flights suspended.

text.p: The Air Force said Tuesday that it had suspended routine training flights of its costly new batwing B-2 stealth bomber.

It said a "precautionary stand-down" of training flights for the 13 radar-evading bombers built so far had been ordered because of a problem with the shaft between the engine and electrical generator in at least one of the planes.
The bombers are built by Northrop Grumman Corp.
"This precautionary stand-down will continue until all aircraft have been inspected and cleared to resume flight training," the Air Force said.
Congress approved funding for 20 of the planes after a battle over costs, now estimated at $44.8 billion. Supporters hope eventually to win funding for 20 more of the aircraft.
